body:
Worker trap (Termal::BarA1, 2026-10-18, met on the w-52222f575b81 carry). TermAl's blobs are LF, but .git/config sets core.autocrlf=true, so a checkout (reset --hard, checkout, apply) writes CRLF files to disk. git diff --cached reads a stat-clean working-tree file instead of its blob. With CRLF files on disk, the staged-diff bytes therefore depend on autocrlf: the Engram schema-1 script (run with core.autocrlf=false) and the pinned `termal.exe review-freeze-check` (repository config, true) compute different fingerprints. The check fails with "review input drifted from the independently supplied fingerprint", although the tree is identical. FIX: before freezing, normalize the changed files on disk to LF (`perl -pi -e 's/\r\n/\n/' FILES`), restage with `git -c core.autocrlf=false add -- FILES` (the tree is unchanged; verify with write-tree), then freeze. The script and the checker then agree. Diagnose by comparing `git -c core.autocrlf=true diff --cached --stat` with the false form: a whole-file rewrite under false means CRLF files on disk. Also: Git Bash `grep -c $'\r'` miscounts CRs; count with `tr -cd '\r' | wc -c`.

VARIANT (Termal::BarA1, 2026-10-19, the w-4d6283a1f1f5 carry onto 89211511): after `git reset --hard NEW` plus `git read-tree -m -u NEW MERGED`, the files that changed between bases are written CRLF and their index stat entries are stale. `git -c core.autocrlf=false diff --stat` then shows whole-file diffs for files you never touched (26 there), so the script and the checker disagree ("drifted") even after LF-normalizing your own changed files. FIX: `git update-index -q --refresh` (with the repository's own autocrlf=true). It only refreshes the stat cache and changes no content; the unstaged diff is then empty under both settings, and the refreeze passes the pinned check. Diagnose with the unstaged `diff --stat` under autocrlf=true vs false.
